They also checked Biography.com and BBC History, which both confirmed 1865.

However, the user noticed that the initial answer given was 1865, but then there was confusion about whether it was 1865 or 1866. I think the mistake might have happened when WebSurfer was trying to open the Royal Family page, which was returning a "Page not found" error. This could have led to confusion or reliance on a conflicting source that suggested 1866, which isn't correct.

So, the mistake agent here is WebSurfer because they couldn't access the Royal Family page to confirm the birth year accurately. The step where this mistake occurred was when they tried to open the Royal Family page, which was step 3 of the instructions. Because of this error, they might have cross-checked with a source that gave the wrong year, leading to the confusion between 1865 and 1866.
